title: Token-bucket rate limiter
statement: Implement a per-client token-bucket rate limiter. Each client's bucket holds at most capacity tokens and starts full; it refills continuously at refill_per_sec tokens per second. Requests [t_ms, client_id, cost] arrive in non-decreasing time order. A request is allowed (return 1) and its cost deducted if the bucket has at least cost tokens; otherwise it's rejected (return 0) and nothing is deducted. Use exact arithmetic (e.g. track millitokens as integers).
hints: Don't run a timer per client: refill lazily when the client's next request arrives.
Store (tokens, last_time) per client; tokens += elapsed × rate, capped.

solution.explanation: The key design move is lazy refill: a bucket's state is (tokens, last update time), and the refill since then is computed on demand. No background timers, so it's O(1) per request. Integer millitokens avoid floating-point drift (the third test is exactly on a boundary). In a distributed system the same state lives in Redis with an atomic script, or approximately in each node with periodic sync. Compare a fixed window (bursty at the edges), a sliding log (exact but O(requests) memory) and a sliding-window counter (a cheap approximation).
